Since PP' is parallel to normal of the plane then

63=b-β-4=c-γ12

Let the point on the circle be cosθ,sinθ,0 and foot of the perpendicular from a point on the circle x2+y2=1,z=0 to the plane 2x+3y+z=6be h,k,w, 

Now using foot of perpendicular formula we get,

h-cosθ2=k-sinθ3=w-01

=-12cosθ+3sinθ-614 ......1

⇒h=cosθ+-22cosθ+3sinθ-614

⇒h=10cosθ-6sinθ+1214 .....2

Now again from equation 1 we get,

k=sinθ-3142cosθ+3sinθ-6

k=5sinθ-6cosθ+1814 ......3

Now eliminating sinθ and cosθ from equation 1 & 2 we get,

5h+6k-122+43h+5k-92=1

⇒5x+6y-122+43x+5y-92=1

Again from equation 1 w==-12cosθ+3sinθ-614 ...4

Now from equation 2, 3 & 4 we get,

questions.solution:
Given planes are:

x-cy-bz=0 ...(i)

cx-y+az=0 ...(ii)

bx+ay-z=0 ...(iii)

Equation of the plane passing through the line of intersection of the plane (i) and (ii) may be taken as:

x-cy-bz+λcx-y+az=0

or  x1+λc-yc+λ+z-b+aλ=0 ...(iv)

If plane (iii) and (iv) are the same, then 

∴  1+cλb=-(c+λ)a=-b+aλ-1 or λ=-a+bcac+b

and λ=-(ab+c)1-a2

∴  -a+bcac+b=-ab+c1-a2

⇒   a-a3+bc-a2bc=a2bc+ac2+ab2+bc

⇒   2a2bc+ab2+ac2+a3-a=0

⇒  a2abc+c2+b2+a2-1=0

⇒  a2+b2+c2+2abc=1
